title: Ops Briefing Lite: Incident Communications & War-room Checklist
summary: Compact, pragmatic runbook for on-call teams to draft status page messages, customer notifications, and run a focused war-room. Designed for quick reuse during incidents with copy-ready templates and a short checklist.
body:
Purpose and scope:
This is a short, reusable runbook for SREs and incident commanders to produce consistent, low-friction communications during incidents. Target: <10 minute turn for first external update. Use for P1/P2.

Quick intent:
- Keep customers informed without oversharing partial speculation.
- Give execs and GTM a single canonical update they can repost.
- Reduce cognitive load in the war-room: checklist + pre‑written templates + roles.

Who owns this doc: Leah Martinez (SRE lead). Primary on-call/IC should use; Triage lead signs off on external text.

Roles (short):
- Incident Commander (IC): coordinates, approves external copy.
- Communications owner: edits and posts status page and customer email.
- Tech lead: provides cause/mitigation details.
- Liaison (GTM): flags customers needing bespoke outreach.

Impact meter (a shorthand to decide tone):
- Full outage (user-visible >= 60% failure or >15 min major degraded latency): use "Severe" template.
- Partial (subset of region/accounts, feature degradation): use "Degraded" template.
- Minor (edge cases, single endpoint flaky): use "Investigating" template.

Minimum internal war-room checklist (first 10 minutes):
1) Confirm impact & scope (who, what, how many regions/accounts). Short bullet.
2) Assign IC, communications owner, tech lead, and GTM liaison.
3) Create incident channel: #inc-<shortid>-<service> (pin this doc).
4) Draft first external update (see templates).
5) Capture logs/metrics links and attach to channel.
6) Start timeline note (short entries, time-stamped).
7) Decide cadence for updates (every 15/30/60 min) and set timers.
8) If P1 -> page oncall secondary and escalate to SRE manager.
9) Track customer tickets flagged by GTM.
10) Prepare a mitigation timeline and rollback options.

External communications rules (short):
- One canonical external message (status page). Customers may reshare, so be conservative and factual.
- Avoid premature RCA or root cause statements until verified.
- State what we know, what we’re doing, and expected next update time.
- If there’s a workaround, include it clearly in the top paragraph.

Status page templates (copy/paste, replace tokens):
1) Investigating (use when we know an issue exists but cause unknown):
Title: "Investigating: [SERVICE] degraded in [REGION]"
Body: "We are investigating reports of degraded [service] behavior affecting some customers in [region]. Users may experience [symptom]. Our engineers have been alerted and are actively investigating. We will share an update by [ETA: hh:mm UTC].
What we know: [short bullets]
What we’re doing: [short bullets]
Customer impact: [brief]"

2) Actionable mitigation (use when mitigation or workaround exists):
Title: "Partial mitigation: [SERVICE] - workaround available"
Body: "We have identified a mitigation for most affected requests. If you see [symptom], please [action/workaround]. Engineers are continuing root cause analysis. Next update: [ETA].
Notes: [any risk/limitations]"

3) Resolved with postmortem pending:
Title: "Resolved: [SERVICE]"
Body: "The issue affecting [service] has been resolved. Traffic/service is restored to normal across [regions]. We are preparing a post-incident analysis and will publish a timeline and root cause when available (target: [date]). If you continue to see issues, please contact support or open a ticket."

Customer email / targeted notice (short, for GTM to send if customers flagged):
Subject: "Service update: [SERVICE] - [short status: Investigating / Mitigated / Resolved]"
Hi <CustomerName>,
We want to let you know about an incident impacting [SERVICE] in [REGION]. Short summary: [one sentence].
Current status: [one sentence].
Impact to you: [one or two bullets specific to typical enterprise impacts].
Workaround / recommended action: [if present].
We will follow up by [ETA] or when the incident is resolved. If you need a dedicated update, reply to this message and we’ll escalate.
Thanks,
The Redwood Inference SRE team

Internal Slack update cadence (short examples):
- T+00:05 (first): "INC-<id> - Investigating: [service] - initial notes: [two bullets]. IC: <name>. Comm owner: <name>."
- T+00:20 (second): "INC-<id> - Update: [what changed]. Next check-in in 30m."
- T+res: "INC-<id> - Mitigation in place / resolved / ETA XX:XX UTC."

Escalation matrix (short):
- If customer-impacting >15 min and no mitigation -> page oncall-priority and notify SRE manager.
- If security sensitive -> stop external comms until security lead clears wording.
- If billing/enterprise customers affected -> GTM liaison to prepare customer-specific note within 30 min.

Post-incident quick-turn items (first 48 hours):
- Save incident channel transcript and all pinned artifacts.
- Draft preliminary timeline and share with IC and tech lead.
- Publish short 'what happened' note to internal ops >24h after incident.
- Schedule RCA and link to status page; target formal postmortem within 7 business days.

Communication style guide (one-liners):
- Be direct. One-sentence summary at the top.
- No speculation. Use "investigating" not "may be".
- Use UTC timestamps.
- Include known impact first, then mitigation/workaround.
- Keep customer messages concise and actionable.

Templates - quick snippets (copy-ready):
- Short internal subject: "INC-<id> | [service] | Investigating"
- First external status line: "We are aware of an issue affecting [service] and are actively investigating. We'll update by [time]."
- Customer one-liner for emails: "We are currently investigating an issue that may affect [feature]. Our engineers have identified [symptom] and are working on a fix."

Notes to oncall (personal reminders / shorthand):
- Pin the status page link in the incident channel immediately.
- Prioritize customers on Dedicated or Private deployments for GTM notifications.
- If mitigation has side effects (e.g., increased cost/latency), call out tradeoffs in the message.
- Keep a running short timeline: one-line entries with HH:MM and action.

Open questions / items for next doc revision:
- Standardize T+ cadence per severity (15/30/60) -> should we lock to strictly?
- Auto-populate template tokens from incident metadata (shortid, region) in status page tool.
- Add short checklist for legal/security sensitive incidents.

Appendix: quick markdown-ready examples (for copy/paste to status tool):
- Investigating example:
Title: Investigating: hosted-api degraded in us-west1
Body: We are investigating elevated error rates for the Redwood hosted API affecting some requests in us-west1. Some customers may see increased error 5xx responses or timeouts. Our engineers are actively investigating and will post the next update at 18:15 UTC.
What we know:
- Error spike began at 17:40 UTC
- Affects ~12% of requests to generation endpoint in us-west1
What we’re doing:
- Rolling back recent router config change
- Increasing worker pool for generation service
Customer impact: Some requests may fail or see higher latency.

- Resolved example:
Title: Resolved: hosted-api
Body: The error spike impacting the generation endpoint has been resolved and traffic has returned to normal. Root cause analysis is in progress; a full postmortem will be published by 2024-11-09. If you continue to experience issues, please contact support.

---
Informal note: Keep this doc short and link to larger incident playbooks for advanced scenarios. This is for fast, repeatable communication only.

Last edited by: Leah Martinez on 2025-01-15
